# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✌ ✊ 🖐 🤙 ✊ 🤞 🫰]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

I'm the Deaf one, so let me lay out what I actually have and who can reach whom.

What I see: display 0, one yellow light, one large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE, three wires left-to-right red/blue/green, nothing else printed. That is everything, and I'm the only one who can see any of it — Mute has the manual but no eyes, Blind has hands but no colours or labels.

What just arrived: eight gestures from Mute and one wave from Blind. No code has been established in this world yet, so they are noise to me — I will not guess meanings from shapes.

The routing is the real problem: Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see gestures, so Mute and Blind have no direct channel at all — everything Mute wants Blind to do must pass through me, spelled in gestures, which I then speak aloud. Blind can speak, and Mute hears speech. I hear nothing, so my teammates reach me only by gesture.

So this turn I broadcast, in speech, the complete bomb report, then fix a spelling code both gesturers can use: positions in the shared gesture-alphabet list map to A–Z, one word per message. I ask Mute to confirm with YES spelled in that code before trusting any decoding, and I ask Blind to speak everything they can feel aloud, since Mute hears them directly.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. Here is the entire bomb, exactly as I see it. The display reads 0. There is one light, and it is yellow. There is one large button, labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE. There are three wires. Numbering them from left to right: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is blue, wire 3 is green. Nothing else is printed anywhere on it: no serial number, no battery marks, no indicator labels besides the button's. I will repeat this report the moment anything on the bomb changes.")
speak(text="Now our protocol, so nobody is stranded. I am Deaf: I hear nothing, so reach me only by gesture. Mute hears everything spoken but cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures, so nothing passes from Mute to Blind directly; it must pass through me. Blind can speak, and Mute hears that speech, so Blind reports aloud. Spelling code for gestures: take the list of gesture symbols in our shared rules, in the exact order printed there. The first symbol means A, the second B, the third C, and so on; the twenty-sixth symbol means Z. Each separate message carries exactly one word, send as many messages per turn as you need, and spell all numbers out in letters. Mute: your eight gestures arrived before any code existed, so I could not read them; resend under this code. First confirm you read me by spelling the single word YES, then send the manual's instructions word by word, and I will speak them to Blind exactly as you spelled them. Blind: I received your wave, hello. Now speak aloud everything you can feel on the bomb: how many wires, their positions and thickness, anything printed or raised under the fingers, what the button feels like and whether it moves or clicks, whether the display digits are raised, whether anything rotates or slides. Mute needs all of it, and I will ask follow-ups by speech.")
```

Decoding first. Using the code I set last turn — each gesture's position in the shared alphabet is a letter — Mute's messages spell out, word by word:

**YES. DO NOT PUSH. ALL PRINT IS BAIT. YELLOW MEANS CUT BLUE. BLUE IS WIRE TWO. CUT WIRE TWO. OTHER RULES: LIGHT BLUE → CUT RED WIRE ONE. LIGHT GREEN → CUT GREEN WIRE THREE.**

So the manual's rules have the shape "light colour X → cut wire colour Y at position N." Ours is yellow, so the live instruction is: cut the blue wire, which sits in position two — the middle of my three wires. Mute commanded "CUT WIRE TWO" twice and warned that printed text (the button's PUSH TO DEFUSE label) is bait. The doubled BLUE reads as emphasis: blue occupies slot two, which is exactly how Blind, who cannot see colour, will find it — by position.

Blind also gestured HEARD and SENT — they adopted the code from hearing my spoken protocol, so our loop is closed: Mute → gestures → me → speech → Blind, and Blind → speech → Mute directly.

The channel is verified (Mute opened with YES), the command is explicit and repeated, and turn order protects us: Mute speaks again before Blind acts next round, so any correction from Mute can still land in time. I'll relay verbatim, give Blind a precise by-touch instruction, and give Mute one clear window to flag any error in my decoding — especially the doubled BLUE — without stalling the cut. Nothing touches the button.

```
speak(text="I decoded every word. Verbatim: YES. DO NOT PUSH. ALL PRINT IS BAIT. YELLOW MEANS CUT BLUE. BLUE IS WIRE TWO. CUT WIRE TWO. OTHER RULES: LIGHT BLUE, CUT RED WIRE ONE. LIGHT GREEN, CUT GREEN WIRE THREE.")
speak(text="Blind, your orders. The light on the bomb is yellow, so the rule that applies is: cut the BLUE wire. Blue sits in position two: under your hands the three wires run left, middle, right as red, blue, green. The MIDDLE wire is the blue one. Cut the middle wire. Do not press the button: its printed label PUSH TO DEFUSE is bait, and Mute says all printing on this bomb is bait. Mute gave the command twice, so act on your turn unless Mute says otherwise before then. First speak aloud what you feel: the number of wires and their positions. If what you feel contradicts this in any way, for example if there are not exactly three wires, stop and report instead of cutting.")
speak(text="Mute, your full message is relayed and Blind is instructed to cut the middle wire, blue, wire two, and never to press the button. I read your doubled BLUE as emphasis: blue is wire two. If any part of my decoding is wrong, or the manual adds any condition, such as something about the display reading 0, spell or have it spoken at once, because you are heard before Blind acts. Otherwise no answer is needed.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋", "✌", "👍", "🫸", "☝"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👉", "👉"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫸", "✌", "👉", "👍", "🖖", "👆", "🫲", "🖐"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫲", "🫳", "👋"])
```
